messages.about.digests_html: The full digests, page by page, are in {link}. To check that a document here is the one you were given, run shasum -a 256 yourfile.pdf and compare.
messages.about.heading: About this archive
messages.about.how_p1_html: These pages were built from the original files with {link}, which reads each document, renders every page, recovers the text — from the file where the file has usable text, and by recognising it from the image where it does not — and writes out a plain, static website. No part of this archive needs a server, an account, or a working internet connection beyond the one that fetched it.
messages.about.how_p2: Recognition is imperfect and this site says where. A page marked unreadable has ink on it that no search will find; a word set with a dotted underline was recognised with low confidence. Where the text and the scan disagree, the scan is the document and the text is our reading of it.
messages.about.how_p3: Redactions were found by looking for solid blocks in the rendered page and filled rectangles in the file, and measured against the inked area of the page rather than its full size. Where an agency printed the exemption it relied on, that code was read off the page and attributed to the box on its line — the line rather than the distance, because a reviewer's stamp goes out in a margin, level with the passage it covers. Where the line settles nothing, the code was counted for the page.
messages.about.keeping_p1: This archive is a folder of ordinary files. It can be copied, mirrored, zipped, put on a memory stick, or re-hosted anywhere that can serve static files, by anyone, without asking us. That is deliberate: an archive that depends on one organisation's funding lasts as long as that funding.

messages.compare.intro: The same documents, produced twice. Below is what one release shows that the other does not — passages an agency covered and then let through, or published and then took back. Nothing here is a summary of anyone's account of these documents; it is a comparison of the pages themselves.
messages.compare.key_corroborated: the box changed and the text agrees. This is the claim.
messages.compare.key_geometry: a box was lifted and nothing legible was found where it had been. Something changed; we cannot say what.
messages.compare.key_suspected: the box changed, but the text under it was also read on the other copy — usually a sign the two scans are not lined up. Shown, not counted.

messages.compare.not_compared_why: Two documents that cannot be aligned produce a comparison that is confidently wrong, so none was made. If you believe these are two releases of the same document, the usual reasons this happens are a re-typed or re-paginated production, a scan too poor to read on one side, or two files that each hold part of the same document.
messages.compare.note_move_budget: {old} in the earlier release and {new} in this one is too many to test for reordering, so pages that merely moved are reported as one removal and one addition.
messages.compare.note_new_unreadable: Recognition failed on this release's copy of this page, so a box that was lifted may have text under it that we could not read.
messages.compare.note_no_stamps: At least one of these productions carries no control numbers, so pages were matched on their content and their position rather than on a stamp.
messages.compare.note_old_unreadable: Recognition failed on the earlier release's copy of this page, so nothing here rests on comparing its text.
messages.compare.note_position: These two pages were matched by their position in the document, not by their text: the earlier release's copy of this page shares too little readable text with this one to identify it. That is usually because it was blacked out. If instead the agency replaced the page, everything below is about two different sheets and is wrong.
messages.compare.note_registration: The black boxes that did not change still sit about {percent} of the page apart on the two scans, so this page's geometry is only approximately registered and the regions below may be off by about that much.
messages.compare.note_renumbered: Both productions stamp control numbers on their pages, and the two sets have nothing in common: the second release was re-numbered. The numbers were therefore ignored, and pages were matched on their content alone.
messages.compare.note_window: Only pages within {window} positions of each other were compared; a page that moved further than that is reported as one removal and one addition.
messages.compare.nothing: Nothing changed. Every document in this release was matched to one in the earlier release, every page was matched to a page, and no black box moved. If you expected an appeal to have produced something, it did not produce it here.

messages.compare.refuse_too_few: only {matched} of {total} pages could be matched to a page in the other release, which is too few to call these two versions of one document.

messages.compare.wrong_absence_html: Absence of a finding is not evidence of no change. A release that was re-typed, re-paginated or re-scanned so differently that the boxes cannot be matched will produce few findings and no warning that there was more to find. The pages that could not be compared are listed above; read them as questions, not as answers.
messages.compare.wrong_hidden_html: Nothing here comes from under a black box. Both releases were read with the same rule the rest of this archive uses: text that a box covers but does not remove is never published, and a build that finds any is stopped. Every passage quoted in this section was visible on paper in one of the two productions.
messages.compare.wrong_link: How this comparison can be wrong →
messages.compare.wrong_ocr_html: A machine read both copies. Text that recognition missed on the earlier copy and caught on this one looks exactly like a disclosure until the black boxes are consulted, which is why they are consulted first and why text alone never counts.
messages.compare.wrong_pages_html: The pages may be mismatched. Deciding that a page of this release is a particular page of the earlier one is an inference. Where a production stamps a control number on every page and both releases use the same numbering, that inference is close to certain. Otherwise it rests on the text, the shape of the page and its position in the sequence, and every page in the tables here carries which of those was used and how strong it was. A page matched at low confidence has nothing claimed about it at all.
messages.compare.wrong_scans_html: The two scans may not line up. Everything here is measured in fractions of a page, so a difference in resolution does not matter — but a different crop or a skew does. Where the black boxes that did not change still sit apart on the two copies, the page says so and by how much.

messages.negative.by_exemption_note1_html: The same rectangles counted rather than drawn. What an exemption is used for is in the size column: a code that removes names takes a line at a time, and a code that removes reasoning takes half a page. Median size is the share of one page the middle box of that group covers; together is all of them added up.
messages.negative.by_exemption_note2: A code printed beside a box belongs to that box. Where an agency printed one code for a whole page and nothing beside the boxes, everything withheld on that page is counted under it — a weaker claim, and the count of those is under the table. Where a page cites several codes and no box carries one, the boxes are counted as uncited, because choosing whichever code is nearest would be inventing a fact.

messages.quality.suspect_body: The recogniser returned something, but it does not read as language, so search results from this page may be wrong and its absence from a search proves nothing. Trust the scan, not the transcription.
messages.quality.suspect_heading: The text on this page is unreliable.
messages.quality.unreadable_body: There is ink on it, but nothing legible came back from the recogniser, so no phrase on this page can be found by searching. The scan itself is unaffected — read it beside this note.
messages.search.heading: Search
messages.search.label: Search these documents

search.noscript_html.one: Search needs JavaScript, which is off in this browser. Everything is still here without it: every page of every document is an ordinary web page with its text on it, and {link} reaches it. Your browser's own find-in-page will search whichever one you open.
search.noscript_html.other: Search needs JavaScript, which is off in this browser. Everything is still here without it: every page of every document is an ordinary web page with its text on it, and {link} reaches all {count} of them. Your browser's own find-in-page will search whichever one you open.

messages.search.placeholder: a name, a phrase, a date
messages.withheld.gaps_heading: Pages that are not here at all
messages.withheld.gaps_note: Where a production stamps a control number on every page, a break in the sequence means pages were withheld in their entirety. Those pages leave no black box to count.
messages.withheld.heading: What was withheld
messages.withheld.intro: Redactions are counted from the documents themselves, not from anyone's summary of them. The percentages below are of inked content — the text and the boxes that replaced it — not of page area, so a page blacked out from margin to margin reads as 100% and not as 63%.
messages.withheld.law_note: Where an agency printed the exemption it relied on, we read it off the page and counted it. A code belongs to the black box on its own line, however far across the page it was printed — a reviewer's stamp sits level with the passage it explains, usually out in a margin. Where that line holds several boxes the nearest of them takes the code, and where none of them is near it the code is counted for the page rather than guessed at. A code with no box on its line is attributed to one right beside it, and otherwise to the page, as is a code printed in a page footer. Choose a code to see the pages it was cited on.

withheld.no_codes.one: No exemption code was printed on these pages, so we cannot say which law was relied on — only that 1 passage was removed.
withheld.no_codes.other: No exemption codes were printed on these pages, so we cannot say which law was relied on — only that {count} passages were removed.

withheld.nothing.one: Nothing on this page is blacked out. That is unusual enough to be worth saying plainly.
withheld.nothing.other: Nothing in these {count} pages is blacked out. That is unusual enough to be worth saying plainly.

messages.withheld.rows_all: Every page with something blacked out on it, most redacted first.

withheld.rows_capped.one: The {shown} most redacted of 1 page that has something blacked out on it, in that order.
withheld.rows_capped.other: The {shown} most redacted of {count} pages that have something blacked out on them, in that order.

messages.withheld.rows_uncited_note: A page with no code beside it is here too: it was withheld under something, and the release does not say what.
messages.withheld.see_negative: See the shape of it — every redaction in this release, drawn at true size →
messages.withheld.showing_html: Showing the pages that cite {code} — {label}. {link}.
messages.withheld.th_label: What it allows to be withheld

notes.about.digests_html: {link} is a link to manifest.json. Keep the shell command inside <span class="mono"> exactly as it is — it is a command a reader types.
notes.about.how_p1_html: {link} is a link to the software's own home page; its text is the product name Stackroom and is not translated.
notes.about.how_p2: 'A word set with a dotted underline' describes how this site marks a word the recogniser was unsure of.
notes.about.how_p3: The same attribution rule as withheld.law_note, in the past tense: this page describes what one particular build did. See that note for the rule.
notes.about.keeping: A section about the archive outliving whoever published it: it can be copied and re-hosted by anyone.
notes.about.language_unknown: Shown where the tool could not tell what language the documents are in.
notes.about.languages_note: {languages} is a list of language names, already joined with commas.
notes.about.th_sha: A column of SHA-256 checksums. The name of the algorithm is not translated.
notes.about.two_digests: Shown on the about page only when safety.strip_metadata rewrote some of the documents, so those rows of the table carry both a sha256 and a published_sha256. {count} is how many of them do. The paragraph exists because an unexplained mismatch between two hashes of the same document is worse than no second hash at all: it has to say the difference is deliberate and say what made it. Note that a form covering more than the number one cannot use a pronoun for the documents - Russian's 'one' also covers 21 - so restructure rather than agree with the count.
notes.about.two_digests_which_html: The sentence after it, saying which digest is which. sha256 and published_sha256 are field names in manifest.json and shasum -a 256 is a command: all three are literal and do not translate, and each keeps its <span class="mono">. {link} is a link to manifest.json, already marked up. Say plainly which number a reader checks against the sender and which one their own shasum will print.
notes.browse.subtitle: {documents} and {pages} arrive already written out.
notes.bytes.b: A file size in bytes. {size} is already written with this locale's separators. Byte units are not usually translated, but do use your alphabet's form if there is one (Russian: Б, КБ, МБ, ГБ).
notes.bytes.tb: A file size in terabytes. Only offline.js reaches this unit, reporting what a browser says it has room for; Translator.bytes() stops at GB.
notes.compare.against: Under the document's title: which release it was compared against. {release} is the earlier release's label, written by the operator — often a noun phrase that already contains the word for 'release' ('the 2019 release'), so a translation that adds its own noun in front produces 'compared against the release the 2019 release'. Quote the label instead, the way the shipped catalogues do.
notes.compare.against_as_html: The same, when the document was called something else in the earlier release. Keep the <span class="cmp-was">.
notes.compare.align_heading: The heading over the table that says which page of this release is which page of the earlier one.
notes.compare.align_note_html: How the pairing was done. The <em> is on the word 'low', which is the confidence label compare.sure_low and has to be the same word. 'Control number' is the stamp on each page of a production.
notes.compare.alt_new: The alt text of a thumbnail of this release's sheet.
notes.compare.alt_old: The alt text of a thumbnail of the earlier release's sheet. It describes the picture for somebody who cannot see it.
notes.compare.blind_heading: The heading over boxes that went away with nothing legible where they had been. Something was released and we cannot say what — the honest form of a non-finding.
notes.compare.blind_no_text: The note beside a finding under the heading compare.blind_heading: a black box went away and the page underneath it, which was read successfully, has nothing legible where the box had been. Lower-case; it sits in a row of small facts.
notes.compare.blind_unreadable: The same slot, for the other reason there is nothing to quote: recognition failed on this release's copy of the sheet, so we cannot say whether anything was released there. Lower-case, same row.
notes.compare.by_document: The heading over the list of documents.
notes.compare.code_change_html: The same passage withheld under one exemption before and another now. {old} and {new} are lists of statutory codes and are not translated; keep both <span class="mono"> wrappers.
notes.compare.codes_label: The same passage withheld under one statutory exemption before and a different one now. 'Exemption' is the statutory ground for withholding — see the note on withheld.under_law.
notes.compare.codes_note: Sits under it. 'Law' here means the specific provision cited, not the statute as a whole.
notes.compare.count_disclosed: One document's tally, in a row of them: how many passages it newly discloses.
notes.compare.count_imposed: The same, counting boxes added. It follows compare.count_lifted in the row and inherits the word 'boxes' from it, so English says only '3 added'. If that does not work in your language, write the noun again.
notes.compare.count_lifted: The same, counting black boxes removed or made smaller.
notes.compare.count_pages_added: The same, counting pages that are in this release and not the earlier one.
notes.compare.count_pages_gone: The same, counting pages that were in the earlier release and are not here.
notes.compare.count_withheld: The same, for passages newly withheld.
notes.compare.description: The page's meta description, which is what a search engine and a chat app show. {old} and {new} are the two releases' labels, which the operator wrote and which are not translated.
notes.compare.diagram_label: The alt text of the diagram of one page — the picture of where the black boxes are — for a reader who cannot see it. {what} is a list of counts joined by compare.evidence_join: '2 redactions lifted, 1 added, 4 unchanged'.
notes.compare.diagram_lifted: One clause of that list: boxes this release no longer draws.
notes.compare.diagram_none: The same alt text when nothing about the boxes changed.
notes.compare.diagram_unchanged: Another clause: boxes that are in the same place in both releases. It follows the others and inherits the noun from them, so English says only '4 unchanged'.
notes.compare.disclosed_heading: The heading over the passages this release printed that the earlier one covered. This is the finding the whole feature exists for; 'disclosed' is the term of art for material an agency has released.
notes.compare.disclosed_intro: The line under that heading. 'In the clear' means not blacked out — printed so it can be read.
notes.compare.disclosed_label: The count that matters most: passages a black box covered in the earlier release and that are printed in the clear in this one. 'Disclosed' is the term of art for material an agency has released. Russian «раскрыто», Ukrainian «розкрито».
notes.compare.disclosed_note: Sits under that count, explaining it in six words.
notes.compare.doc_description: That page's meta description. {old} and {new} are release labels and are not translated.
notes.compare.doc_title: The name of one document's comparison page, which goes inside title.join with the collection's name.
notes.compare.doubted_summary: The summary line of a collapsed block. The passages inside it are shown and never counted. 'The box changed but the text does not agree' is the failure of the corroboration rule in compare.how_rule_html.
notes.compare.evidence_and: What separates the last two items of such a list: 'control numbers, text and filename'. A language that does not join a list with a word can set this to the same thing as compare.evidence_join.
notes.compare.evidence_dominated: Shown against a pair the aligner kept at low confidence because one of the two pages resembles some other page more. It is a whole clause rather than a term, and it appears in the same list as the terms above.
notes.compare.evidence_filename: Another: the two files have similar names.
notes.compare.evidence_identical: The two files are the same file, byte for byte, so no other evidence was needed.
notes.compare.evidence_image: Another: the two renderings of the sheet look alike as pictures.
notes.compare.evidence_join: What separates the items of a list of evidence, and of the clauses in compare.diagram_label. A locale that punctuates lists differently should change it here.
notes.compare.evidence_layout: Another: the ink sits in the same places on the sheet, whatever it says.
notes.compare.evidence_order: Another: the words run in the same order. It separates two pages that share a vocabulary from two pages that share a text.
notes.compare.evidence_out_of_order: This pair was found by a second pass over the pages the main alignment could not place, so it sits at different positions in the two releases.
notes.compare.evidence_position: The weakest: nothing about the content decided this, only where the page sits in the sequence.
notes.compare.evidence_same_filename: Another, and stronger: the two files have exactly the same name.
notes.compare.evidence_stamp: The strongest: both productions stamp the same control number on the page. See the note on withheld.gaps_note for the term.
notes.compare.evidence_stamp_differs: The opposite, and a reason to doubt a pairing: both pages carry a control number and they are not the same one.
notes.compare.evidence_stamps: Evidence for pairing two documents rather than two pages: their control numbers overlap.
notes.compare.evidence_text: One kind of evidence for matching two pages or two documents: the words on them are largely the same.
notes.compare.exemption_added_html: An exemption code printed on this page in this release and not in the earlier one. This is a page-level fact and a weaker one than a code changing on a single box, and it is worded as the weaker fact. Keep the <span class="mono">.
notes.compare.exemption_removed_html: The reverse: a code the earlier release printed on this page and this one does not.
notes.compare.finding_blind: Appended to a corroborated passage whose other copy could not be read at all, so the black box is the only evidence. Lower-case, same row.
notes.compare.finding_doubted: Appended to a doubted passage, saying why it is doubted. Lower-case: it sits at the end of a row of small facts.
notes.compare.geometry: The arithmetic under each page: how many black boxes there are between the two copies and what became of them. Every placeholder is a count that arrives already written with this locale's separators, and the six words after the colon are the six kinds of change. Keep all six.
notes.compare.geometry_noise: Follows it: how many words on this page the two recognitions read differently, with no change in any box. 'Recognition' means OCR, and 'are not counted as anything' means these words produce no finding in either direction.
notes.compare.had_been_under_html: The same, for a box that was lifted with nothing readable underneath.
notes.compare.heading: The heading of the comparison section. 'Release' here is the batch of documents an agency handed over in answer to a request — the term of art your transparency community uses for a production, not a software release. See the note on compare.release_old.
notes.compare.headline: The heading over the six or seven big numbers. 'The headline' as a newspaper would use it — the finding in one line.
notes.compare.how_heading: The heading over the rule that decides what gets counted. It is above the findings on purpose and should not read as a footnote.
notes.compare.how_noise: How many words the two scans were simply read differently on, with no change in any black box. Publishing this number is the honesty of the page: it lets a reader judge how noisy the recognition was. 'Recognition' means OCR.
notes.compare.how_rule_html: The rule the whole feature rests on: a finding needs a change in the black boxes AND a change in the text, agreeing. Keep the <strong> on the phrase that carries the claim, wherever it lands in your word order.
notes.compare.identical: Said when the two files are byte-for-byte the same. 'Nothing in it was reconsidered' is the point: the agency answered again without reviewing anything.
notes.compare.identical_short: This document is the same file in both releases, down to the byte, so there is nothing to compare.
notes.compare.imposed_label: Black boxes added or enlarged since the earlier release. 'Imposed' because somebody decided to cover something that had not been covered.
notes.compare.intro: The standfirst under that heading. 'Covered and then let through' and 'published and then took back' describe the two directions a redaction can change in; keep both directions distinct, because the second one is the more serious finding.
notes.compare.key_corroborated: The legend entry that follows the badge, so the sentence reads 'corroborated — the box changed and the text agrees.' It starts lower-case for that reason.
notes.compare.key_geometry: The same, for the no-text badge.
notes.compare.key_suspected: The same, for the suspected badge. 'The two scans are not lined up' means the two images of the same sheet are offset from each other, so a box's coordinates do not land on the same words.
notes.compare.legend_imposed: The same legend: an area this release covers and the earlier one did not. 'Since then' refers to the earlier release just named in the previous entry.
notes.compare.legend_kept: A legend entry under the diagram of one page. The diagram draws both releases' black boxes on one outline of the sheet: solid for an area this release still covers.
notes.compare.legend_lifted: The same legend: an area the earlier release covered and this one does not. {release} is the earlier release's label.
notes.compare.lifted_label: A count of black boxes that went away or got smaller, whether or not any text could be read where they had been. A weaker fact than a disclosure and worded as one: this counts boxes, the two above count passages.
notes.compare.look_at_scan: A link to the page's own scan, so a reader can look at what the machine could not read. Lower-case: it sits at the end of a row of small facts.
notes.compare.matched: A ledger entry: how many pages of this release were matched to a page of the earlier one.
notes.compare.matched_note: Sits under that count. {total} is the number of pages in this release, already written with this locale's separators.
notes.compare.matched_to_html: Said when a document has a different title in the two releases: this is what it was called before. Keep the <span class="cmp-was">.
notes.compare.matched_to_on_html: The same, with the evidence for the pairing named. {evidence} is a list of already-translated terms joined by compare.evidence_join and compare.evidence_and — 'control numbers and text'.
notes.compare.no_code: Stands in for the list of codes when the release cited none. It says the release printed no code, not that no exemption was relied on.
notes.compare.not_compared_html: The warning at the top of a document that was not compared. {reason} is one of the compare.refuse_* sentences and arrives already written, beginning lower-case. Keep the <strong>.
notes.compare.not_compared_why: The paragraph under it: why refusing is the right answer, and what usually causes it.
notes.compare.note_move_budget: Said when there are too many unplaced pages to test them all for reordering. {old} and {new} arrive already written and already pluralised, from compare.unmatched_pages.
notes.compare.note_new_unreadable: A warning: recognition failed on this copy, so a lifted box may be hiding text nobody has read.
notes.compare.note_no_stamps: A note on the whole comparison: at least one production stamps no control numbers, so pages were matched on content and position.
notes.compare.note_old_unreadable: A warning: recognition failed on the earlier copy of this sheet, so only the black boxes are evidence.
notes.compare.note_position: The strongest warning on a page, shown first: these two sheets were paired on their position alone. The last sentence says plainly what it would mean if the pairing is wrong, and should not be softened.
notes.compare.note_registration: A warning above one page's findings: the black boxes that did not change do not sit in the same place on the two scans, so every coordinate on this page is approximate. {percent} is a share of the page, already written.
notes.compare.note_renumbered: A note on the whole comparison: both productions stamp control numbers and the two sets do not overlap, so the numbers were ignored.
notes.compare.note_window: A note above the alignment table for a long document: only pages near each other in the sequence were compared, because comparing every page against every page is too expensive past a size.
notes.compare.nothing: The whole section when the two releases turn out to say the same thing. The last sentence is deliberate: a reader who came here after an appeal deserves to be told plainly that the appeal produced nothing, rather than shown an empty page.
notes.compare.nothing_changed: This document was compared and nothing about it changed.
notes.compare.now_under_html: The same, for a passage this release has covered.
notes.compare.only_heading: The heading over pages that exist in one release and not the other.
notes.compare.only_new: A tag on a document that exists only in this release.
notes.compare.only_new_note: Pages added since the earlier release. 'Resembles' is deliberately weak: the tool is saying it found no similar page, not that no such page exists.
notes.compare.only_old: A tag on a document that exists only in the earlier release.
notes.compare.only_old_note: Pages that were in the earlier release and are not here. The second sentence keeps the reader from over-reading the first.
notes.compare.page_n: A page, named inside a table cell or a list item. English writes it lower-case here because it is not the start of a sentence; page.n is the same thing at the start of one.
notes.compare.page_n_old: A page of the earlier release, which has no page in this archive to link to.
notes.compare.pages_added_label: Pages in this release with no counterpart in the earlier one.
notes.compare.pages_gone_label: Pages in the earlier release with no counterpart here. A page that disappears between two releases of one document is a question worth asking, which is why it is counted beside the others.
notes.compare.pages_heading: The heading over the page-by-page findings.
notes.compare.pair_evidence: What the tool matched the two files on. {evidence} is a list of already-translated terms — see compare.evidence_join.
notes.compare.read_document: A link from the comparison to the document itself. The arrow is part of it; reverse it for a right-to-left language.
notes.compare.refuse_no_pages: One of the compare.refuse_* sentences, which are dropped into compare.not_compared_html after 'These pages were not compared.' They all begin lower-case and are written as the second half of that sentence.
notes.compare.refuse_nothing_alike: Another: nothing in one release looks like anything in the other.
notes.compare.refuse_order: Another, and the subtlest: both copies read fine and the words do not run in the same order. It is the test that separates two versions of one document from two documents built out of the same boilerplate.
notes.compare.refuse_too_big: Another: too many page pairs to score. {old} and {new} are page counts and {limit} is the ceiling, all already written with this locale's separators.
notes.compare.refuse_too_few: Another: some pages matched, not enough of them. {matched} and {total} are counts.
notes.compare.refuse_weak: Another: the pages matched, but only weakly. {score} is a similarity between 0 and 1, written with this locale's decimal separator.
notes.compare.refused_tag: A badge on a document the tool declined to compare, because it could not convince itself the two files are two versions of one document. Refusing is the correct outcome and the word should not sound like a failure.
notes.compare.release_digest_html: Appended after that, when the release has a digest: the first sixteen characters of a SHA-256 over the whole release, so two people can tell they are talking about the same batch of files. It begins with a separator and a space; keep the <span class="mono">.
notes.compare.release_meta: Under a release's name: how big it is. {pages} and {documents} arrive already written out and already pluralised ('1,204 pages', '16 documents'), so this message is only the frame that joins them.
notes.compare.release_new: The other side: the release this archive is built from and publishes. It is also the column heading over the pages a reader can actually open.
notes.compare.release_old: Names one side of the comparison: the batch of documents the agency produced first. 'Release' and 'production' are the same thing in this practice — the material handed over in answer to one request. Russian «выдача», Ukrainian «добірка», Polish «udostępnienie». Not a software release.
notes.compare.sheet_caption: The caption under one of those two thumbnails: which release it is, then how much of it is blacked out. {state} arrives already written — one of compare.state_almost_all, compare.state_clear, withheld.row_share or compare.tag_gone.
notes.compare.short: The name of the comparison section, used as a breadcrumb and inside the page title. The long form is compare.heading.
notes.compare.state_almost_all: The state of one sheet, in the caption under its thumbnail: ninety per cent or more of its content is blacked out.
notes.compare.state_clear: The same caption for a sheet with no black boxes on it at all.
notes.compare.sure_certain: One of four confidence words in the alignment table, strongest first: certain, high, medium, low. They are read as a scale, so keep them short and keep them ordered.
notes.compare.sure_low: The weakest of the four, and the one that carries a rule: a page matched at this level has nothing claimed about it. The word also appears inside compare.align_note_html and compare.wrong_pages_html and must be the same word in all three.
notes.compare.tag_added: A badge in the alignment table: this page of the current release has no counterpart in the earlier one.
notes.compare.tag_corroborated: A one-word badge beside a finding: the black box changed and the text agrees. This is the word the counts above are counts of, so it must match compare.key_corroborated and js.compare.corroborated. In a legal sense: confirmed by a second, independent piece of evidence.
notes.compare.tag_geometry: A one-word badge: a black box was lifted and nothing legible was found underneath. Literally 'there is no text here to quote', not 'this is not text'.
notes.compare.tag_gone: A badge: this page of the earlier release has no counterpart here. It is also the caption under a missing thumbnail.
notes.compare.tag_moved: A badge: this page was matched, but it sits at a different position in the two releases.
notes.compare.tag_suspected: A one-word badge: something changed in the boxes, but the text does not corroborate it. Shown and never counted. 'Suspected' as an investigator would use it — not yet established.
notes.compare.th_confidence: A column heading: how much that number is worth. The four answers are compare.sure_certain and its neighbours.
notes.compare.th_evidence: A column heading: which kinds of evidence the pairing used.
notes.compare.th_new: A column heading. The other column is headed with the earlier release's own label, which the operator wrote.
notes.compare.th_score: A column heading: a number from 0 to 1 saying how alike the two pages are.
notes.compare.this_release: Used as {release} in compare.sheet_caption for the current release's own thumbnail, where the earlier one is named by its label. Lower-case because it is inside a caption.
notes.compare.truncated: Said when a document has more changed pages than the forty diagrams the page will carry. The last sentence is the important one: nothing was dropped from the totals, only from the pictures.
notes.compare.unmatched_pages: Pages the alignment could not place. Used twice inside compare.note_move_budget, once for each release.
notes.compare.unmatched_share: How much of a doubted passage was not found on the other copy of the page. {percent} arrives already written with this locale's percent sign.
notes.compare.unpaired_heading: The heading over documents that were left over on either side.
notes.compare.unpaired_note: Why a document can be left over. 'Re-cut into different files' means the same pages redistributed among a different set of PDFs, which this tool cannot detect.
notes.compare.unusable: Pages that were matched too weakly for anything to be claimed about them. They are shown in the alignment table and nothing is said about their contents.
notes.compare.was_page: Beside a page's number: which page it was in the earlier release.
notes.compare.was_under_html: In that row: the exemption the earlier release cited for the box that covered this passage. Keep the <span class="mono"> around the codes, which are statutory codes like (b)(5) and are never translated.
notes.compare.withheld_heading: The heading over passages the earlier release printed and this one covers.
notes.compare.withheld_intro: The line under it, including the sentence that says where the quoted text came from. That sentence is load-bearing: the archive is quoting material the agency itself published once, not material recovered from under a box.
notes.compare.withheld_label: The opposite and rarer finding: text the earlier release printed and this one covers. 'Withheld' is the term of art for material an agency removed — see the note on nav.withheld and use the same word your catalogue uses there.
notes.compare.words: How long a quoted passage is, in words. It sits in a row of small facts under the quotation.
notes.compare.wrong_absence_html: The fourth, and the one a reader is most likely to get wrong: finding nothing is not evidence that nothing changed. Keep the <strong>.
notes.compare.wrong_heading: The heading of the section that says how this comparison can be wrong. It is a section and not a footnote, and it is above the fold on a phone.
notes.compare.wrong_hidden_html: The fifth: nothing quoted here was recovered from under a black box. This is a promise about the tool's behaviour and its wording matters — every passage on these pages was visible on paper in one of the two releases. Keep the <strong>.
notes.compare.wrong_link: A link to that section from the foot of a document's own comparison page. The arrow is part of it; reverse it for a right-to-left language.
notes.compare.wrong_ocr_html: The third: recognition failing on one copy and succeeding on the other looks like a disclosure. Keep the <strong>.
notes.compare.wrong_pages_html: The first caveat: the pairing of page to page is an inference. 'Control number' is the stamp a production puts on every page (a Bates number) — see the note on withheld.gaps_note. Keep the <strong> on the opening claim and the <em> on the word 'low', which is the confidence label from compare.sure_low and must match it.
notes.compare.wrong_scans_html: The second: the two images of one sheet may be cropped or skewed differently. Keep the <strong>.
notes.count.documents: A count of documents, used on its own inside a longer sentence (see footer.built and browse.subtitle). It must stand alone grammatically.
notes.count.pages: A count of pages, used on its own inside a longer sentence and also as the whole reading of the strip of ticks. It must stand alone grammatically.
notes.doc.download: A link to the original file, byte for byte, as it was received. 'The original' is load-bearing: the point is that the reader can check this site's renderings against the file.
notes.doc.gaps: A break in the production's control-number sequence — a stamped number that is missing, which almost always means pages withheld in their entirety.
notes.doc.gaps_body_html: {ranges} is a list of control numbers, already marked up. 'Withheld in full' means the whole page was removed, not part of it.
notes.doc.numbered_html: {prefix} is the common start of the control numbers stamped on this document's pages, e.g. 'OCA-2018-04412-'. Keep the <span class="mono"> and the ellipsis.
notes.doc.redacted: Pages in this document that have something blacked out on them. Appears in a run of short facts separated by dots.
notes.doc.thumb_withheld: Under a page thumbnail: how many separate blacked-out areas are on that page.
notes.empty.pictorial: The page is a photograph, a map or a drawing — it was read correctly, and there was nothing on it to read.
notes.empty.unrendered: Shown where a page produced neither an image nor any text. The middle clause is the point: this is not a claim that the page is blank, it is an admission that the build could not read it.
notes.footer.built: The colophon on every page. {documents} and {pages} arrive already written out ('16 documents', '1,204 pages'); {date} is written with this locale's date pattern; {version} is a version number like 0.1.0.
notes.footer.digest_html: {digest} is the first 16 characters of a SHA-256 hash of the source documents. 'Source digest' is a checkable fingerprint of what went in, not a summary. Keep the <span class="mono">, which sets the hash in a monospaced face.
notes.home.ledger_unreadable_note: Sits under a number, as its explanation: '12 — pages search cannot find text on'. The number is not in this string; your language may still need the count to choose the right form, which is why it has plural forms.
notes.home.ledger_withheld_collection_note: Sits under the second percentage in the front page's Withheld cell, as its explanation: '3.9% — of everything in this release'. The figure above it is a share of the redacted pages only; this one is a share of the whole release. Both are printed because either alone misleads: one page withheld in full out of a thousand is 100% of that page and 0.1% of the release. Keep it parallel with home.ledger_withheld_note - each names the denominator of the number above it - and use the same words for the inked content as withheld.intro does. 'Release' is the batch of documents an agency handed over; see docs/TRANSLATING.md.
notes.home.ledger_withheld_note: Sits under a percentage, as its explanation: '12.4% — of the content on 318 redacted pages'. It is a fragment, and it may need to be a whole clause in your language.
notes.home.no_about_body_html: Addressed to the person who built the site, not to a reader. Keep the file name about.md inside the <span> exactly as it is; it is a filename, not a word.
notes.home.see_withheld: A link. The arrow is part of it — in a right-to-left language, point it the other way (←).
notes.home.top_exemption: The statutory ground the agency cited most often when withholding material.
notes.js.cite.control_comma: The same, after a comma, for js.cite.note.
notes.js.cite.control_paren: The control number in parentheses, dropped into js.cite.plain. The leading space is deliberate and belongs to this message.
notes.js.cite.control_semi: The same, after a semicolon, for js.cite.markdown.
notes.js.cite.digest: The SHA-256 clause, dropped into js.cite.plain and js.cite.note. "SHA-256" is the name of the algorithm and does not translate.
notes.js.cite.digest_both: The SHA-256 clause when the published file and the file the agency sent are two different files, which is what safety.strip_metadata produces. {sha} is the digest of the file a reader can download from this archive — the number `shasum -a 256` will print for it, and the one an editor checks — and {source} is the digest of the file as it arrived. Both are the first sixteen characters. Say which is which; an unlabelled second number in a citation is worse than none. "SHA-256" is the name of the algorithm and does not translate.
notes.js.cite.digest_both_markdown: The same clause for Markdown, where each digest is set in backticks so it renders as code. Keep both pairs of backticks.
notes.js.cite.digest_markdown: The same clause for Markdown, where the digest is set in backticks so it renders as code.
notes.js.cite.foot: The sentence under the panel. The SHA-256 in a citation is of the original file the agency released, not of the web page — which is the whole point of publishing it.
notes.js.cite.foot_stripped: Replaces js.cite.foot under the panel when the citation carries two digests. It has to answer the question an editor will otherwise ask — why does this archive publish a file whose digest is not the one it says the agency sent — and say plainly which of the two to check.
notes.js.cite.formats: The accessible name of the group of three format choices.
notes.js.cite.link: The button beside it that copies this page's address.
notes.js.cite.link_highlight: What that button says instead when the reader arrived on a highlighted passage, because the link it copies will keep the highlight. The label is a promise about what is about to be copied.
notes.js.cite.manual: Said when the browser refuses the clipboard — a mirror served over plain http, or an archive opened from a stick. {keys} is the key combination, ⌘C or Ctrl C, and is not translated.
notes.js.cite.markdown: The same citation as Markdown. Keep the [text](url) shape — a reader is going to paste this into a document that will render it.
notes.js.cite.markdown_name: A citation as a Markdown link. The word is the name of the format and usually stays as it is.
notes.js.cite.note: The same citation shaped like a footnote. The quotation marks around the title are the ones your language uses for a title.
notes.js.cite.note_name: A citation shaped like a footnote in a piece of scholarship.
notes.js.cite.open: The button under a page's metadata line that opens the citation panel.
notes.js.cite.plain: The citation itself, in prose. {control} and {digest} are already-written phrases that are empty when there is nothing to say; {url} is the page's address and {day} is the date it was read, in ISO order. Reorder as your language's citation practice wants.
notes.js.cite.plain_name: A citation to paste into ordinary prose.
notes.js.cite.text_label: The accessible name of the box holding the citation.
notes.js.compare.all: Show every finding, including the ones the comparison is unsure of. This is the default, deliberately: a page that quietly starts filtered is a page that quietly omits.
notes.js.compare.corroborated: Show only findings the comparison will stand behind. "Corroborated" means confirmed by more than one piece of evidence.
notes.js.compare.hidden: Said whenever the filter changes, so nothing is ever hidden without the page saying so. {what} is a list of the two clauses below, joined with ribbon.join.
notes.js.compare.hidden_findings: The other: individual passages the comparison doubts.
notes.js.compare.hidden_pages: One of those clauses: pages that went away because nothing on them survived the filter.
notes.js.compare.legend: The accessible name of the filter on a comparison page, which sets what the page shows.
notes.js.compare.show: The visible word in front of the two choices. It ends in a colon.
notes.js.compare.showing_all: Said instead when nothing is hidden.
notes.js.keys.actual_size: What 1 does: show the scan at its own pixel size.
notes.js.keys.next_page: What j does on a page of a document.
notes.js.keys.next_withheld: What r does: fly to the next redacted area on the page.
notes.js.keys.or: Joins two keys that do the same thing in the shortcut sheet - "j or →". The keys themselves are never translated; this word between them is. Keep it short: it sits in a narrow column beside the key names.
notes.js.keys.pan: What the arrow keys do in the full-size view.
notes.js.keys.scan_full: What z does: open the scan at full size.
notes.js.keys.step_page: What j and k do there.
notes.js.keys.this_list: What ? does: open the sheet the reader is looking at.
notes.js.keys.whole_page: What 0 does: fit the whole page in the window.
notes.js.keys.zoom: What + and − do in the full-size view. These are the descriptions in the shortcut sheet; the keys themselves are not translated.
notes.js.lens.close: The button that closes the full-size view.
notes.js.lens.fit: The button that fits the whole page in the window. One word if your language has one.
notes.js.lens.opened: Announced when the full-size view opens. Escape is a key name.
notes.js.lens.stage_label: The accessible name of the scan itself inside the full-size view. {label} is js.scan.page_of_document. The two gestures are named because they cannot be guessed from looking at a rectangle.
notes.js.lens.void: Announced when one of those areas is reached. {index} is which one and {count} is how many there are; both forms must print {count}.
notes.js.lens.void_cited: The same, where the agency printed an exemption code beside it. {area} is js.lens.void and {codes} is a list of statutory codes.
notes.js.lens.withheld_button: The visible label on the button that steps through the redacted areas. {count} is how many there are on this page, in parentheses; both forms must print it.
notes.js.lens.withheld_button_label: Its accessible name, which says what pressing it does.
notes.js.lens.zoom_in: The accessible name of the + button.
notes.js.lens.zoom_out: The accessible name of the − button.
notes.js.negative.cell_label: The accessible name given to one page in the field when a keyboard reaches it. {meta} is the page's metadata line, read back off the index list below the picture.
notes.js.negative.filtered: Announced when the reader picks out one exemption code. {label} is the code and its gloss. The state of the control is said in words as well as shown in colour, because colour alone is not a state.
notes.js.negative.no_code_here: Said in the tooltip over a rectangle on the negative that carries no exemption code. Singular, about one box; negative.no_code_label is the plural form used in the table.
notes.js.negative.tip_where_html: The first line of that tooltip: which document and which page. Keep the <strong> around the title.
notes.js.offline.failed: Said when some files could not be fetched. A partial store still reads.
notes.js.offline.file: One of three honest refusals. This one is for an archive being read from a folder on the reader's own disk, where the whole thing is already offline and a service worker is neither possible nor needed. "file://" is a URL scheme and is not translated.
notes.js.offline.files: A count of files, used inside the sentences here. Every form must print {count}.
notes.js.offline.full: Said when the device ran out of room part-way. {done} is a plain number and {total} a js.offline.files phrase; see the note on js.offline.partial about word order.
notes.js.offline.insecure: The second refusal: a browser will not store a site served over plain http. Not a failure of this archive, and the sentence says so.
notes.js.offline.interrupted: Said when storing ended for a reason nobody can name.
notes.js.offline.killed: Said when the reader themselves switched it off with ?stackroom-offline=off in the address. Leave that query string exactly as it is — it is typed, not read.
notes.js.offline.killed_by_publisher: Said when whoever published the archive has switched offline storage off by publishing a `sw-kill` file. The reader is told, because their stored copy has just been deleted.
notes.js.offline.load_new: The button that switches to the new version.
notes.js.offline.newer: Said when the archive has been rebuilt and republished since this device stored it.
notes.js.offline.no_store: Said when registering the worker failed for a reason that is nobody's fault — a private window, an enterprise policy, storage switched off. A statement, not an error.
notes.js.offline.partial: Said when some of the archive is stored. {held} is a plain number, {files} an already-pluralised js.offline.files phrase, {percent} a percentage. If your language inflects a noun after a preposition - so that "of 202 files" cannot take a phrase that already carries its own numeral - reorder the sentence so the phrase stands on its own: the Russian, Ukrainian and Polish catalogues all do.
notes.js.offline.preparing: Said while the worker is installing and has not yet reported what it holds.
notes.js.offline.remove: The button that deletes the stored copy.
notes.js.offline.starting: Said while the service worker is being registered.
notes.js.offline.stop: The button that stops storing. There is no timeout: storing a gigabyte over a phone connection is a legitimate hour, and this is the way out.
notes.js.offline.stopped: Said when the reader pressed Stop.
notes.js.offline.store_all: The button that fetches the whole archive. The size is on the button before a single byte is fetched, deliberately: a collection can be gigabytes.
notes.js.offline.storing: Said while the archive is being stored, before the first progress report. {percent} is a percentage.
notes.js.offline.storing_progress: The same line once the worker is reporting. {size} is how much has arrived.
notes.js.offline.tight: Appended to js.offline.partial when the browser is offering less room than the archive needs. {line} is that sentence and {size} is how much room is left.
notes.js.offline.unsupported: The third: the browser has no service workers at all.
notes.js.offline.whole: Said when every file is stored. {size} is a file size, {files} an already-pluralised js.offline.files phrase.
notes.js.palette.button_label: The accessible name of the masthead button that opens the palette. The visible label is the keyboard shortcut, which is not translated.
notes.js.palette.capped: Said when more rows match than the palette will draw. {shown} is how many are on screen and {count} is how many matched. Both forms must print {count}: it is a number the reader is being told about.
notes.js.palette.control_numbers: The sub-line on the row that matches a document by the control-number prefix stamped on its pages. "Control number" is the term of art; see the note on doc.numbered_html.
notes.js.palette.destinations: The accessible name of the list of results inside the palette.
notes.js.palette.exemption: The sub-line on a row for a statutory exemption code, where the build has no plain-language gloss for that code. {pages} arrives already pluralised from count.pages.
notes.js.palette.exemption_glossed: The same row where a gloss exists. {label} is the plain-language explanation of the statute, which stays in English deliberately — see docs/TRANSLATING.md on exemption glosses.
notes.js.palette.front: The sub-line on the row that goes to the archive's front page.
notes.js.palette.gap: The sub-line on a row for a break in a document's control-number sequence, which usually means pages withheld in full.
notes.js.palette.keys_html: The line of keys under the palette. The <kbd> elements are the keys themselves and their contents are symbols, not words; the words between them are yours. Keep all three <kbd> elements.
notes.js.palette.label: The accessible name of the command palette, which jumps to a document, a page, a control number or an exemption code. It is not search: search asks what a page says, this asks where a thing is.
notes.js.palette.nothing: Said, once, when nothing in the archive matches what has been typed.
notes.js.palette.placeholder: The text in the empty box. It names the three kinds of thing the palette can find.
notes.js.palette.recent: The sub-line on a row the reader has been to before, when nothing else is known about it.
notes.js.palette.recent_of: The same, keeping what the row was. {what} is another of these sub-lines — "Section", "12 pages".
notes.js.palette.section: The sub-line on a row that goes to one of the standing pages — Documents, Search, Withheld, About.
notes.js.palette.stamp_page: The sub-line on a row found by typing a control number: which page of which document carries that stamp.
notes.js.passage.cite: The citation under a copied quote. {control} is an already-written js.cite.control_paren phrase, empty when there is no control number.
notes.js.passage.copy_link: Its first button: a URL that highlights exactly the selected words, on this page, boxed on the scan.
notes.js.passage.copy_quote: Its second: the words themselves, with the citation and the permalink under them, so a writer does not have to retype a sentence out of a public record.
notes.js.passage.field_label: The accessible name of the fallback field offered when the browser has no clipboard.
notes.js.passage.label: The accessible name of the little bar that appears when a reader selects words in the transcription.
notes.js.passage.link_copied: What the first button says after it worked.
notes.js.passage.quote: The whole copied quote: the words, a blank line, then the citation and the link. The quotation marks are the ones your language uses. Keep the two newlines.
notes.js.passage.selected: Announced to a screen reader when a selection is made. Tab is a key name and is not translated.
notes.js.passage.this_document: Stands in for the document's title in a quote's citation when the page does not carry one.
notes.js.passage.withheld: Written into a copied quote where a redaction interrupts it. Absence is content: a quote that closes over the hole reads as a continuous sentence the document does not contain. Keep the brackets, or your language's equivalent.
notes.js.passage.withheld_code: The same, where the agency printed the exemption code beside the box. {code} is that code.
notes.js.prefs.forget: The button that deletes everything this archive has stored in the browser — the theme, the size, and where the reader had got to in each document.
notes.js.prefs.label: The accessible name of that button. It is a panel of two settings: theme and text size.
notes.js.prefs.note: The promise under the panel: the settings live in this browser's own storage and are never sent anywhere.
notes.js.prefs.open: The label on the reading-settings button in the masthead. Two letters of your own alphabet, one capital and one small, as a compact sign for "type" — Cyrillic "Аа", Greek "Αα". Not an abbreviation of any word.
notes.js.prefs.size: The legend over the three text sizes.
notes.js.prefs.size_large: One step up. There is no step down: nobody reading a photocopy has ever wanted it smaller.
notes.js.prefs.size_largest: Two steps up, and the last one.
notes.js.prefs.theme: The legend over the light/dark choice.
notes.js.prefs.theme_dark: Light text on a dark ground.
notes.js.prefs.theme_system: Follow whatever the reader's operating system is set to. The default.
notes.js.resume.forget: The button beside it that deletes that memory.
notes.js.resume_html: Offered once, in the flow of the document page, when the reader has been reading this document before. {href} is a relative link to the page they had reached. Keep the <a> around whatever names the page.
notes.js.scan.open_full: The button under a scan that opens it full size. Built by a script, so a page with no scripting never shows a control that would do nothing.
notes.js.scan.page_of_document: The accessible name of the full-size view: which page of which document is in it.
notes.js.scan.this_document: Stands in for a document's title where the page does not carry one.
notes.js.scan.where_untitled: The line in the full-size view's bar naming the page, where the document has no title. Where it has one, page.where is used instead.
notes.js.search.caveat: The standing note above the results whenever any page is missing from the index. {covered} is how many pages pagefind actually indexed, {total} is how many there are and {count} is the difference; every form that covers more than one number must print {count}. Do not say the missing pages are ink nobody could recognise: a blank page and a page that is a photograph are both read perfectly well and neither has any text to index. Name all three possibilities or none.
notes.js.search.failed: Said when it did not come back.
notes.js.search.hits: The result count, and the one message on the page a screen reader is told about on every keystroke. {query} is what the reader typed, in your language's quotation marks.
notes.js.search.loading: Said while the search index is being fetched — about 200 KB, and only once somebody puts the cursor in the box.
notes.js.search.more: Said under a long list of results. {shown} is how many are drawn and {count} how many matched; both forms must print {count}. The inner quotation marks are the ones a reader would type to search for an exact phrase, so leave them as plain " marks.
notes.js.search.none: Said when nothing matched. The count is of pages searched, which is the honest frame: it says how much was looked at.
notes.js.search.none_quoted: Appended when the query contains quotation marks, because an exact phrase has to match exactly. {none} is whatever came before it.
notes.js.search.none_unreadable: Appended to it when some pages are missing from the index. {none} is that sentence. A search that quietly omits 200 pages it has no text for tells the reader a phrase is not in the archive, which may be false and is the worst thing a search over public records can do. It says what happened - nothing was indexed - rather than why, because the reason differs from page to page.
notes.js.search.result_where: The link on one result: which page of which document it is.
notes.js.search.searching: Said while a query is running.
notes.js.search.too_short: Said for a query below the minimum length. Latency tracks the number of hits rather than the size of the archive, so a one-letter query is not a fast search of everything, it is a frozen tab.
notes.js.search.unavailable: Said when it did not load. Search is an accelerant, never a prerequisite: every page is still an ordinary web page.
notes.js.strip.dark: The same, for a page the recogniser could make nothing of. Shorter than key.dark for the same reason.
notes.js.strip.part: The state word on the hover tile over the strip of page ticks, for a page with something blacked out on it. Shorter than key.part because it sits in a tile a thumbnail wide.
notes.js.viewer.keyboard: The heading of the keyboard-shortcut sheet, opened with ?.
notes.js.viewer.matches: Announced to a screen reader when a search hit is highlighted on a page.
notes.key.dark: A page whose text could not be recognised, so a search will never find anything on it. The scan is still readable by eye. Not 'unreadable' in the sense of illegible handwriting.
notes.key.readable: The legend beside the strip of ticks on the front page. One word per state of a page. Keep them short — they sit in a row.
notes.key.void: A page with no ink on it at all.
notes.language.en: Language names shown on the about page, listing what the documents are written in. Write them in your own language and in your own conventions for capitalisation — Russian and Ukrainian do not capitalise language names.
notes.meta.document: The <meta name="description"> of a document's page, never displayed on screen — it is what a search engine or a chat app shows when somebody links to this archive. {pages} arrives already written out.
notes.meta.page: The <meta name="description"> of one page of one document.
notes.nav.compare: One word in the site's navigation for the section that compares two releases of the same documents. It labels a section, not an action — the reader is not being asked to compare anything. Keep it short; it sits in a row with the other navigation words.
notes.nav.skip: The first link on every page, for a keyboard or screen-reader user: it jumps past the masthead to the document. 'Document' here means the archived page being read, not the HTML document.
notes.nav.top: Follows an upward arrow. 'Back to the top of the page.'
notes.nav.withheld: One word in the site's navigation for the page that counts and explains redactions. In freedom-of-information practice this is the standard term for material an agency has removed — use your jurisdiction's equivalent, not a literal translation of 'withheld'. Russian: «Изъятия». Ukrainian: «Вилучення».
notes.negative.arrange: A control above the picture, offering different arrangements of the same rectangles. A verb or a noun, whichever is idiomatic for a control.
notes.negative.arrange_code: The arrangement that groups every rectangle under the exemption cited for it. Same term of art as nav.withheld's "exemption": the statutory ground for withholding.
notes.negative.arrange_code_caption: The sentence under that control. "What an exemption is actually being used to remove" is the finding this arrangement exists to make visible.
notes.negative.arrange_page: One of the three arrangements the reader picks between, and the default. "Page order" means the redactions are drawn where they sat on the page they came from.
notes.negative.arrange_page_caption: The sentence under the control saying what that arrangement is for.
notes.negative.arrange_size: The arrangement that puts every rectangle in one run, largest first.
notes.negative.arrange_size_caption: {largest} and {smallest} are already-written phrases from negative.share_* - "12% of the page", "under a tenth of a percent of the page" - so the frame is yours to reorder.
notes.negative.band_code: The heading drawn inside the picture above each exemption's band of rectangles. {extent} is a negative.extent_* phrase - "12 pages' worth".
notes.negative.band_size: The single band heading in the by-size arrangement.
notes.negative.blind_dark_body: {count} is how many such pages there are in the release.
notes.negative.blind_dark_heading: Fourth entry: pages the text recogniser could make nothing of.
notes.negative.blind_gaps_body: {count} is the number of breaks in the control-number sequence; {pages} is an already-written negative.blind_gaps_pages phrase, or negative.blind_gaps_pages_unknown where the stamps could not be counted.
notes.negative.blind_gaps_heading: First of the seven "what this picture cannot show" entries. "Withheld in full" means the page was never released at all, so there is no black box to draw.
notes.negative.blind_gaps_pages: How many pages those breaks account for, as a clause that drops into negative.blind_gaps_body.
notes.negative.blind_gaps_pages_unknown: The same clause with no number, used when the control numbers are not arithmetic enough to count.
notes.negative.blind_invisible_body: The most important sentence on the page: it says what the whole picture is blind to.
notes.negative.blind_invisible_heading: Seventh and last entry, and the one that always appears. It is about the kinds of removal that leave no shape on the page to find.
notes.negative.blind_odd_body: {count} is how many. The claim is that those pages' rectangles are true to each other but slightly small against the rest of the field.
notes.negative.blind_odd_heading: Sixth entry: pages of a different shape from the rest, drawn smaller so they fit the grid.
notes.negative.blind_solid_body: {count} is how many of them; {pages} is an already-pluralised count.pages phrase for the number of pages drawn in the picture.
notes.negative.blind_solid_heading: Second entry: pages that are almost entirely black.
notes.negative.blind_uncoded_body: {count} is how many rectangles carry no code. Two cases at once: nothing was printed on the box's line or beside it, and the ambiguous case where the code on that line is level with several boxes and near none of them, which is counted for the page rather than attached to a guess.
notes.negative.blind_uncoded_heading: Third entry. "No law printed beside them" means nothing on the box's line, and nothing beside it, named a law that could be attributed to it - see the note on negative.blind_uncoded_body.
notes.negative.blind_unrendered_heading: Fifth entry: pages that produced no image at all, so nothing on them could be measured.
notes.negative.by_exemption_note1_html: Keep the three <em> elements. 'Median size' and 'together' are the names of two table columns and must match negative.th_median and negative.th_together exactly.
notes.negative.description: The meta description of the negative page. {collection} is the archive's title.
notes.negative.everything: The first button in that control: show every redaction, dim nothing.
notes.negative.extent_page: The same, when the run comes to about one page.
notes.negative.extent_pages: A run of redactions added up and said as an amount of paper. {pages} is a number to one decimal place, two or more.
notes.negative.extent_share: The same, below a page. {percent} is a whole number of percent.
notes.negative.extent_tiny: The same, below a tenth of a percent.
notes.negative.footer_html: {link} is a link whose text is negative.withheld_link.
notes.negative.heading: The name of the page that draws every redaction and nothing else — as in a photographic negative, where what is dark is what was there. If that metaphor does not carry into your language, choose one that does rather than translating the word.
notes.negative.incomplete_body: {drawn}, {cells}, {total_cells} are counts already written out; {share} is a percentage. The page is admitting that it is not showing everything, which is the point of the sentence — do not soften it.
notes.negative.inherited: A box that carries a code printed for the whole page rather than beside the box itself — a weaker claim about which law was used, and the sentence says so.
notes.negative.label_code: The aria-label on the by-exemption arrangement. {groups} is a list of negative.label_code_group phrases joined with "; ".
notes.negative.label_code_group: One entry in that list. {code} is a statutory code like (b)(5), or the negative.no_code_short phrase where none was printed.
notes.negative.label_code_join: What goes between two entries in the by-exemption picture's spoken label. A semicolon and a space in English, because the entries themselves contain commas. Arabic and Greek use their own semicolon; ribbon.join is the same decision for a plainer list.
notes.negative.label_page: The aria-label on the picture itself: the whole field read as one sentence for somebody who cannot see it. {pages} and {documents} arrive already pluralised from count.pages and count.documents. {count} is the number of redactions.
notes.negative.label_page_dropped: Appended to negative.label_page when the release was too big to draw whole.
notes.negative.label_page_tail: The last sentence of the picture's label, pointing at the list underneath it.
notes.negative.label_size: The aria-label on the by-size arrangement. {largest} and {smallest} are negative.share_* phrases.
notes.negative.no_code_label: The label in the table for the group of redactions that had no exemption code printed beside them. It is usually the largest group in a release, which is itself the finding.
notes.negative.nothing_drawable: Redactions were counted, but none of them has a measurable rectangle, so there is nothing to draw. The last sentence blames the tool, not the documents, and should keep doing so.
notes.negative.pick_out: A control that dims every redaction except the ones cited under one exemption. 'Pick out' as in 'single out', not 'choose'.
notes.negative.share_large: The same, for one percent and up. {percent} is a whole number of percent. It is a separate key from negative.share_small because a language may want a different form of words at the two magnitudes; if yours does not, translate both the same way.
notes.negative.share_none: How one rectangle's share of its page is said, when it rounds to nothing at all. Used by the page and by the tooltip in negative.js, which recomputes the share from the drawing.
notes.negative.share_small: The same, for a share under one percent. {percent} arrives already written with this locale's decimal mark and percent sign, to one decimal place.
notes.negative.share_tiny: The same, for a share below a tenth of a percent. Said in words rather than as "0.0%", which reads as a measurement failure.
notes.negative.th_median: A column heading: the middle value of the group's box sizes, as a share of one page. Must match the words used inside negative.by_exemption_note1_html.
notes.negative.th_together: A column heading: all the boxes in this group added up, as pages' worth. Must match the words used inside negative.by_exemption_note1_html.
notes.page.dimensions: The page's real size in typographic points, as printed. Do not convert to millimetres — this is the measurement in the file.
notes.page.heading_html: The heading of one page of a document. Keep the <span>, which sets 'of {total}' smaller; move it wherever your language puts it.
notes.page.no_image: Shown in place of the scan when the page produced no image at all. The last clause matters: the downloadable original is the only remaining record of that page.
notes.page.prev: A link to the previous page. The arrow is part of the string; in a right-to-left language it points the other way and goes on the other side.
notes.page.redactions_with_share: {percent} is already written with a per-cent sign and this locale's spacing. 'Of this page withheld' means the share of the page's inked content that was removed, not the share of its area.
notes.page.source_embedded: The text beside the scan came from the PDF's own text layer.
notes.page.source_ocr: The text beside the scan was produced by recognising the image, not read out of the file.
notes.page.where: The middle of the pager, saying where in the document the reader is.
notes.page.withheld_bar: The accessible name of the black bar that stands in for a redacted passage in the transcription. It is the only piece of interface text inside the element the search index reads, and it is safe there because an aria-label is an attribute and contributes no token: see tests/test_i18n.py, which indexes the same page with an English label, a Russian one, a longer Russian one and none at all and gets byte-identical indexes, against a control that puts the same words in as text and moves every position after them. Keep it to a word or two - a screen reader reads it in the middle of a sentence.
notes.page.withheld_bar_coded: The same, where the agency printed the exemption beside the box. {label} is the statutory gloss, which stays in English deliberately - see docs/TRANSLATING.md.
notes.page.withheld_under: Introduces a list of statutory exemption codes and their meanings. It ends in a colon and the list follows.
notes.quality.suspect_body: The important claim is the last one: what came back is not trustworthy, so a *failed* search on this page proves nothing about the page.
notes.quality.unreadable_body: 'The recogniser' is the OCR software. 'The scan' is the photograph of the page.
notes.ribbon.dark: As ribbon.part. 'Search cannot read' them — the ink is there, the recognised text is not.
notes.ribbon.end: The list, terminated. Change the full stop if your language ends a sentence differently.
notes.ribbon.join: What separates the items of that list. A locale that separates list items differently should change it here.
notes.ribbon.part: Read out to a screen reader as part of a list describing the strip of ticks: '16 pages, 4 partly withheld, 1 withheld in full.' This item is a bare count plus a description, and it has to work in a list.
notes.ribbon.with_here: The reading of the strip, then a sentence saying which page the reader is on. Reorder if that reads better in your language.
notes.search.noscript_html: Shown only when JavaScript is off. {link} is a link whose text is search.noscript_link. The claim matters: the archive is fully readable without search.
notes.search.placeholder: The grey text in the empty search box. It is an example of what to type, not an instruction.
notes.title.join: The <title> of a page that is not the front page: the page's own name, then the collection's. Reorder or change the separator if your language reads titles the other way round.
notes.title.page_join: The <title> of one page of one document: page name, document name, collection name.
notes.withheld.gap_one_html: One missing control number. Keep the <span class="mono">.
notes.withheld.gap_range_html: A run of missing control numbers, first to last.
notes.withheld.gaps_heading: Pages that were removed in their entirety, so they leave no black box to count and are known only from the break in the numbering.
notes.withheld.heading: The page that counts and explains what an agency removed. See the note on nav.withheld for the term of art.
notes.withheld.intro: 'Inked content' is the text and the black boxes together, as opposed to the whole area of the paper. 100% and 63% are illustrative numbers inside the sentence — rewrite them with your locale's separators if you use different ones.
notes.withheld.law_note: The attribution rule in the order the code applies it: the line first, then proximity, then silence. 'On its own line' is vertical overlap and nothing else — a stamp out in a margin is on the line of the passage it explains however far across the page it sits, and that is the layout most FOIA releases use. 'Near' is about 40pt on Letter. Where a line holds several boxes and none is near the code, nothing is attributed: the code is counted for the page, because naming one of them would be a guess.
notes.withheld.ledger_boxes_note: 'Black boxes' is literal: each separate rectangle drawn over the page was counted.
notes.withheld.ledger_pages_note: Sits under a count: '318 — of 2,041, or 16%'.
notes.withheld.no_code_printed: This page was withheld under something and the release does not say what.
notes.withheld.no_codes: The agency withheld material without printing which exemption it relied on. 'Passages' means stretches of text, not sections of a statute.
notes.withheld.row_title: The link to one page of one document: '{title}, page 7'.
notes.withheld.rows_capped: {shown} is how many rows are listed and {count} is how many pages have redactions in the whole release. The list is capped, and this sentence is the admission of it.
notes.withheld.see_negative: A link to a page that draws every redaction at true size. The arrow is part of it; reverse it for a right-to-left language.
notes.withheld.showing_html: Shown when the reader has chosen one exemption code. {code} is the statutory code, {label} is its plain-language gloss, {link} is a link back to the unfiltered list. Keep <span class="mono"> around the code.
notes.withheld.th_label: A table heading: what this statutory exemption permits an agency to keep back.
notes.withheld.unknown_code: Stands in for an exemption's plain-language gloss when the code is not in the vocabulary for the configured jurisdiction. It says the code was printed and we cannot explain it, not that the code is invalid.
